specialistCandidates.name: Social / Communal Anarchism
specialistCandidates.description: A family-level experimental affinity for anti-authoritarian, communal, and federated social organization. It does not make mutualism, market anarchism, syndicalism, anarcho-communism, or a single transition strategy a required subtype.

specialistCandidates.name: Anarcho-Communism
specialistCandidates.description: Communal ownership and anti-authoritarian federation.

specialistCandidates.name: Individualist Anarchism
specialistCandidates.description: Anti-authoritarian self-direction and voluntary association without a single required economic program.

specialistCandidates.name: Market Anarchism
specialistCandidates.description: An anarchist family anchor for voluntary exchange and non-state coordination, without deciding among capitalist, mutualist, or counter-economic variants.

specialistCandidates.name: Mutualism (family-level)
specialistCandidates.description: A family-level affinity for reciprocal exchange, federated association, and opposition to privilege; it does not identify Proudhonian, Tuckerite, Labadie-line, Swartz-associated, or later mutualist and left-market variants—or affiliation with C4SS or any writer.

specialistCandidates.name: Anarcho-Syndicalism
specialistCandidates.description: Worker organization and direct industrial action under anarchist commitments.

specialistCandidates.name: Anarcho-Capitalism
specialistCandidates.description: Private property and market exchange without a state.

specialistCandidates.name: Minarchism
specialistCandidates.description: A minimal state limited to protective and adjudicative functions.

specialistCandidates.name: Deep Ecology
specialistCandidates.description: Strong independent moral standing for nonhuman nature.

specialistCandidates.name: Degrowth Green
specialistCandidates.description: Democratic reduction of material throughput in affluent economies.

specialistCandidates.name: Ecosocialism
specialistCandidates.description: Ecological transformation joined to collective ownership and anti-capitalist politics.

specialistCandidates.name: Ecomodernism
specialistCandidates.description: Ecological improvement through innovation, infrastructure, and high-capacity institutions.

specialistCandidates.name: Green Capitalism
specialistCandidates.description: Market investment and regulation as the main route to ecological transition.

specialistCandidates.name: Social Democracy
specialistCandidates.description: Reformist welfare and labor politics within a mixed economy.

specialistCandidates.name: Democratic Socialism
specialistCandidates.description: Democratic control or social ownership pursued through pluralist and accountable institutions, with variation over reform and transition.

specialistCandidates.name: Marxian Socialism
specialistCandidates.description: A non-Leninist Marxian family centered on class analysis and social ownership, without requiring a party-state model.

specialistCandidates.name: Market Socialism
specialistCandidates.description: Social ownership combined with market exchange or competition.

specialistCandidates.name: Guild Socialism
specialistCandidates.description: Democratic worker control and public or social ownership organized through self-governing functional associations.

specialistCandidates.name: Council Communism
specialistCandidates.description: Worker councils and direct democratic control of production and politics.

specialistCandidates.name: Syndicalism
specialistCandidates.description: Union organization and direct industrial action as the route to social transformation.

specialistCandidates.name: Maoism
specialistCandidates.description: Revolutionary party organization, mass mobilization, and centralized transition.

specialistCandidates.name: Trotskyism
specialistCandidates.description: Revolutionary Marxism emphasizing international transformation and party strategy.

specialistCandidates.name: Conservative / Prudential Conservative
specialistCandidates.description: Broad prudential continuity and gradual institutional change.

specialistCandidates.name: Social Conservatism
specialistCandidates.description: Moral and family traditionalism as a cross-cutting political commitment.

specialistCandidates.name: National Conservatism
specialistCandidates.description: National continuity joined to conservative institutional politics.

specialistCandidates.name: Liberal Conservatism / Conservative Liberalism
specialistCandidates.description: Constitutional liberty and markets combined with social and institutional continuity.

specialistCandidates.name: Neoconservatism
specialistCandidates.description: Modern U.S. conservative internationalism with an assertive foreign-policy orientation.

specialistCandidates.name: Islamic Democratic Constitutionalism
specialistCandidates.description: Popular sovereignty and constitutional competition interpreted through Islamic legal and ethical traditions.

specialistCandidates.name: Political Islam
specialistCandidates.description: Political projects that make Islamic identity or law central to state and movement politics.

specialistCandidates.name: Theocratic Politics (religious-legal authority)
specialistCandidates.description: A family-level experimental affinity for final religious authority over civil-law legitimacy. It does not identify a religion, clerical office, constitutional form, or treatment of minorities.

specialistCandidates.name: Hindutva
specialistCandidates.description: A majoritarian or civilizational account of Indian national identity centered on Hindu cultural belonging.

specialistCandidates.name: Zionism
specialistCandidates.description: A family of Jewish national self-determination projects with divergent territorial and constitutional variants.

specialistCandidates.name: Religious Nationalism
specialistCandidates.description: An umbrella fusion of religious identity and national goals whose institutional forms vary over law, citizenship, authority, and minority rights.

specialistCandidates.name: Technocratic Centralism
specialistCandidates.description: Centralized expert administration insulated from ordinary electoral pressure.

specialistCandidates.name: Cyberocracy
specialistCandidates.description: Governance through cybernetic information systems and algorithmic administration.

specialistCandidates.name: Techno-Anarchism
specialistCandidates.description: Decentralized technology and cryptography used against centralized control.

specialistCandidates.name: Accelerationism
specialistCandidates.description: Strategic intensification of technological or social change to transform existing institutions.

specialistCandidates.description: A post-capitalist accelerationist current that seeks to redirect technological and economic capacities beyond capitalist social relations.

specialistCandidates.name: Right Accelerationism
specialistCandidates.description: A market-intensifying accelerationist current associated with deepening competition, technological disruption, and the weakening of existing political arrangements.

specialistCandidates.name: Technology-Centered Accelerationism
specialistCandidates.description: A technology-first accelerationist current whose political-economic destination is less specified than its commitment to intensification.

specialistCandidates.name: Dataism
specialistCandidates.description: An epistemic and cultural orientation that gives data-driven systems privileged interpretive authority.

specialistCandidates.name: Absolute Monarchism
specialistCandidates.description: Hereditary authority with concentrated sovereign power.

specialistCandidates.name: Traditional Monarchism
specialistCandidates.description: Hereditary authority grounded in historical and social continuity.

specialistCandidates.name: Constitutional Monarchism
specialistCandidates.description: Monarchy constrained by constitutional and elected institutions.

specialistCandidates.name: Libertarian Municipalism
specialistCandidates.description: Municipal democracy and confederal self-government.

specialistCandidates.name: Democratic Confederalism
specialistCandidates.description: Decentralized, pluralist, and confederal democratic organization.

specialistCandidates.description: Treats patriarchy and male dominance as a distinct structural system, with sexuality, reproduction, and family relations central sites of political power.

specialistCandidates.description: Explains gender domination through the interaction of patriarchy with class, property, paid labor, unpaid care work, and social reproduction.

specialistCandidates.name: Anarcha-Feminism
specialistCandidates.description: Treats patriarchy as intertwined with state and other hierarchical domination and favors decentralized, anti-authoritarian forms of liberation and organization.

specialistCandidates.name: Ethnonationalism
specialistCandidates.description: Defines nationhood primarily through inherited descent and culture and gives political weight to congruence between the state and the historic core nation.

specialistCandidates.name: Multiculturalism
specialistCandidates.description: Supports recognition and accommodation of cultural difference within shared citizenship, including differentiated rights or self-government where justified.

specialistCandidates.name: Black community-autonomy orientation
specialistCandidates.description: Emphasizes Black community autonomy, institution-building, self-reliance, and collective power without requiring territorial separation or independent statehood.

specialistCandidates.name: Black separatist self-determination orientation
specialistCandidates.description: Combines Black collective autonomy with a stronger preference for territorial separation, independent political authority, or separate statehood.

specialistCandidates.description: Treats settler-colonial authority and dispossession as continuing structures and emphasizes resurgence, refusal, land-based political relations, and rebuilding Indigenous institutions on their own terms.
